M.P. Heard on I.A No.22384/2022, an application under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to appellant - Prakash Tekam arising out of judgment dated 20/01/2022 delivered in S.T. No.54/2020 by Additional Sessions Judge, Pandhurna, District Chhindwara.
The appellant has been convicted under Sections 376 (2)(m) and 307 of IPC to undergo RI for Life with fine of Rs.5000/- and R.I. for seven years with fine of Rs.2000/-, with default stipulations.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that incident of sexual assault had allegedly taken place on 05.08.2018, but the FIR was lodged on 24.08.2018.
The victim could not depose her statement in the Court, because she died in normal course in between.
The bamboo 'danda', which is allegedly recovered from the appellant, did not have any stains etc. on the basis of which it can be said to be an incriminating material.
He by placing reliance on statements of PW/5, PW/6 and PW/14 submits that it cannot be said that there is clinching evidence against the appellant.

Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that the Doctor (PW/14) deposed that the person, who brought the injured victim for treatment informed her that she was suffering from 'Mirgi' and fell down in an agricultural field and sustained injuries.
He also submits that FSL report is negative.
Thus, he prayed for suspending the remaining jail sentence of appellant.
Learned Government Advocate opposed the prayer for grant of bail and suspension of sentence on the basis of objection.
A perusal of the judgment and record shows that the victim was sexually assaulted on 05.08.2018 and in addition a bamboo 'danda' was inserted in her anus because of which severe injury was caused.
The victim remained unconscious for about 8 days and was required to undergo an surgery.

Dr.
Bhumika Jaiswal (PW/14) categorically deposed that injury on the person of victim could have been caused by 'danda'.
Prima facie there exists strong circumstantial evidence against the appellant.
In the manner, this heinous crime was committed and in view of prima facie evidence on record, we are not inclined to suspend the remaining jail sentence of appellant.
Accordingly, I.A No.22384/2022 is dismissed.
